newsitem.title: USA: Abbott files for Norvir pediatric labeling.
newsitem.headline: Abbott files for Norvir pediatric labeling.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc said Thursday it filed with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for expanded labeling for its drug, Norvir, to cover treatment of children with HIV and AIDS.
The drug and healthcare products company said there are no drugs in Norvir's class, known as protease inhibitors, that are approved in the United States for use in children.
Data supporting the FDA submission are from an ongoing Phase I/II pediatric study being done at the National Cancer Institute in collaboration with Abbott, the company said.
"Interim results from the study indicate that Norvir can increase patients' CD4 cell counts and can decrease the amount of HIV circulating in the blood," Abbott said.
The data are scheduled to be presented Saturday at a medical conference in Washington, D.C., the company said.
In March last year, the FDA cleared Norvir for treatment of human immunodeficiency virus infection in patients where therapy is warranted.

"We are pleased to be able to take what we learned from the rapid development of Norvir in adults and apply it to the treatment of children," said Andre Pernet, vice president of pharmaceutical products research and development at Abbott.
"As a result, we were able to seek pediatric use of Norvir very quickly," Pernet said.
Shares in Abbott were off 1/2 at 55-7/8.
